info.name: SuprSend APIs
info.description:
**SuprSend API** enables you to add a powerful notification engine to your product. SuprSend has all the features set which enable you to send notifications in a reliable and scalable manner, as well as take care of end-user experience, thereby eliminating the need to build any notification service in-house. We have backend SDKs available in popular programming languages:

- [Java](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/java-sdk)
    
- [Python](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/python-sdk)
    
- [Node JS](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/nodejs-sdk)
    
- [Go](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/go-sdk)
    

If your backend system is programmed in any other language, you can use our REST-ful APIs to programatically integrate with SuprSend notification engine.

If you are new to SuprSend, you can start by understanding the [core concepts](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/templates) first.

item.name: Workflows

request.description:
## Request Body Params

_**workflow**_ : workflow_slug | string | required field. You can get workflow slug from workflow settings on SuprSend dashboard.

_**recipients**_: array of objects | required. List of recipients to be notified. You can either add recipient as array of distinct_ids or array of recipient objects. You can add up to 100 recipients in a single API.

_**actor**_: json object | required. Includes distinct_id and properties of the user who performed the action. You can use it for cross-user notifications where you need to include actor properties in the notification template. Actor properties can be added as $actor..

_**data**_: json object. Variable data required to render dynamic template content or workflow properties like dynamic delay or channel override in send node.

_**tenant_id**_: string. String identifier of the brand/tenant this workflow is associated with. Used to trigger multi-tenant notifications.

_**$idempotency_key**_: string. Idempotency_key (valid for 24hrs).

## Headers

_**authorization:**_ suprsend APIs use bearer authorization. to send a successful request, one muse set the correct the _api_key_ value in the variables. To learn more about how to generate the _api_key_ refer [this.](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/api-keys)

request.description:
API to dynamically create and trigger a single step workflow.

## Request Body Params

**name**: string | required. Unique name of the workflow. The workflow name should be easily identifiable for your reference at a later stage. You can see workflow-related analytics on the workflow page (how many notifications were sent, delivered, clicked or interacted).

**template**: string | required. Unique slug of the template created on SuprSend dashboard. You can get this by clicking on the clipboard icon next to the Template name on SuprSend templates page.

**notification_category**: string | required. Used to apply user category level [preferences](https:///docs/user-preferences) on notification trigger. Default: `transactional`.

**users**: array of objects | required. Array object of target users. Each user object must include:

- **distinct_id**: string | required. Unique identifier of the user.
    
- **$channels**: array of strings | optional. Send notification on selected channels in user profile. Following channel keys can be used - `email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `androidpush`, `iospush`, `slack`, `webpush`.
    
- **$email**: array of strings | optional. To trigger notification on a particular email.
    
- **$sms**: array of strings | optional. Send SMS on a particular number.
    
- **$whatsapp**: array of strings | optional. Send WhatsApp on a particular number.
    
- **$androidpush**: array of strings | optional. Send Android push on the given push token.
    
- **$iospush**: array of strings | optional. Send iOS push on the given push token.
    
- **$slack**: array of objects | optional. Slack channel configuration. Can be configured using:
    
    - User email with access token
        
    - User member ID with access token
        
    - Slack channel ID with access token
        
    - Incoming webhook URL
        
- **$ms_teams**: array of objects | optional. Microsoft Teams channel configuration. Can be configured using:
    
    - Conversation ID with tenant ID and service URL
        
    - User ID with tenant ID and service URL
        
    - Incoming webhook URL
        

**data**: json object | optional. Variable data required to render dynamic template content or workflow properties like dynamic delay or channel override in send node. Can include:

- **$attachments**: array | optional. Use this key to pass email attachment in the trigger. You can either pass attachment as a publicly accessible URL (no limit on file size) or as a base64-encoded file (limit < 50KB).
    

**delivery**: json object | optional. Delivery instructions for the workflow. You can set [Smart Delivery](https:///docs/smart-delivery) preference by setting `"smart": true`. Includes:

- **smart**: boolean | optional. You can enable smart delivery by setting it true. Default: `false`.
    
- **success**: string | optional. Success event for stopping further notification in case smart is set to true. You can set notification status like delivery, interaction or custom success event. Default: `seen`.
    
- **time_to_live**: string | optional. Time window to define delay between subsequent channel trigger in case of smart delivery. Delay = `time_to_live / (number_of_channels - 1)`. Format - `XXdXXhXXmXXs` or if its number (n) then delay is in seconds (n).
    
- **mandatory_channels**: array of strings | optional. Channels on which notification has to be sent immediately in case of smart delivery. Following channel keys can be used - `email`, `sms`, `whatsapp`, `androidpush`, `iospush`, `slack`, `webpush`.
    

**delay**: string | optional. Workflow will be halted for the time mentioned in delay, and become active once the delay period is over. Format - `XXdXXhXXmXXs` or if its number (n) then delay is in seconds (n).

**trigger_at**: string | optional. Trigger workflow on a specific date-time. Format - date string in ISO 8601 e.g. `"2022-08-27T20:14:51.643Z"`.

**tenant_id**: string | optional. String identifier of the tenant this workflow is associated with. Used to trigger multi-tenant notifications.

**$idempotency_key**: string | optional. Unique identifier of the request (deduplicates request for 24hrs).

## Headers

**authorization**: SuprSend APIs use bearer authorization. To send a successful request, one must set the correct api_key value in the variables. To learn more about how to generate the api_key refer [this](https:///reference/authentication).

**Content-Type**: `application/json`

item.description: Workflow is the notification powerhouse where you define the logic and stitch individual pieces together, like [user](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/users), [template](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/templates), [vendor](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/vendors), and [preferences](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/preferences), to deliver notifications to the end user. The workflow logic is designed on the platform and can be triggered using one of the 2 methods: [Direct workflow trigger via API](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/trigger-workflow-api): It is a straightforward way to get started, as you can include recipient channel information directly in the API call and doesn't require prior user creation to initiate the notification. It is best suited for backend triggers such as authentication, and verification notifications, where dynamic user channel information or sensitive data needs to be passed at the time of sending. [Event Based trigger](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/event-api): For other transactional usecases where the event is user action based and the events are generated using our frontend SDKs where user creation happens before hand or passing events and user properties from third-party data platforms like [Segment](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/segment), then event-based trigger would be a better choice. [Learn more about workflows](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/workflows)

item.description:
The event (referred to as event_name) is a string describing an event. Events are also used to trigger workflows designed on SuprSend Platform. All you have to do is send the event to SuprSend platform and the associated workflows will be triggered.

[Learn more about events here](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/events)

item.name: Users

request.description:
API to list cursor-based paginated list of users in your workspace.

## Query Parameters

**limit**: integer | optional. Maximum number of records per page. Default: `10`.

**before**: string | optional. Cursor for the previous page. Use the `before` value from the previous response's `meta` object to fetch the previous page of results.

**after**: string | optional. Cursor for the next page. Use the `after` value from the previous response's `meta` object to fetch the next page of results.

## Headers

**authorization**: SuprSend APIs use bearer authorization. To send a successful request, one must set the correct api_key value in the variables. To learn more about how to generate the api_key refer [this](https:///reference/authentication).

**Content-Type**: `application/json`

## Response

The API returns a cursor-based paginated response with the following structure:

**meta**: object. Metadata related to pagination.

- **count**: integer. Total number of records available.
    
- **limit**: integer. Maximum number of records per page.
    
- **has_prev**: boolean. Indicates if there is a previous page.
    
- **before**: string | null. Cursor for the previous page.
    
- **has_next**: boolean. Indicates if there is a next page.
    
- **after**: string. Cursor for the next page.
    

**results**: array. List of user objects. Each user object includes:

- **distinct_id**: string. Unique identifier of the user.
    
- **properties**: object. User properties (simplified).
    
- **created_at**: string (date-time). Timestamp when the user was created.
    
- **updated_at**: string (date-time). Timestamp when the user was last updated.
API to fetch user object by passing it’s unique `distinct_id`

## **Request Body Params**

_**distinct_id:**_ string | required. distinct_id is the unique identifier of recipient who should receive the notification. The user will be created with this identifier on suprsend, and if the user with this distinct_id already exists, the properties passed in this request will be updated on the subscribers profile.

_**$user_operations:**_ json object

_**$set:**_ nested json object . This contains the key value pairs of the properties that need to be updated on th distinct_id, for example "name": "user".

_**$unset:**_ nested json object . Use this to remove properties from user profile. Define the property keys to be removed as "$preferred_language"

_**$append:**_ nesed json object. Use this to add communication channels in user profile. Following channel keys: `$email`, `$sms`, `$whatsapp`, `$androidpush`, `$iospush`, `$slack`, `$webpush`, `$ms_teams`. Add channel as {"$email":"[user@example.com](https://mailto:user@example.com)"}

_**$remove:**_ nesed json object. Use this to remove communication channels from user profile. Following channel keys: `$email`, `$sms`, `$whatsapp`, `$androidpush`, `$iospush`, `$slack`, `$webpush`, `$ms_teams`. Define channel as {"$email":"[user@example.com](https://mailto:user@example.com)"}

## Headers

_**authorization:**_ suprsend APIs use bearer authorization. to send a successful request, one muse set the correct the _api_key_ value in the variables. To learn more about how to generate the _api_key_ refer [this.](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/api-keys)

item.description:
Users represent a person who will receive the notification. SuprSend identifies a user by a unique identifier `distinct_id` and creates a profile for each user identified by this id.

All the channel information like email id, phone number, and push tokens are attached to the user profile which in turn is used to trigger communication on the given channels.

[Learn more about users](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/users)

## Create / Update Users

To create and update users on SuprSend, you can send `$user_operations` event to us. All changes can be combined in one API call in an easy to replay format to us. Following operations are supported in `$user_operations`:

- `$append` - Add communication channel in user profile.
    
- `$remove` - Remove communication channel from user profile
    
- `$set` - Set User properties like user location, preferred_language etc.
    
- `$unset` - Unset existing user properties
    

You can create a user and add channels and properties to their profile with a [single API](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/update-user-profile) call to SuprSend, similar to sending an event.

item.description:
Preferences define what kind of notifications your recipients should receive and on which channel. By default, user preferences are fetched from Organization and Brands' default preference until the recipient overrides it.

[Learn more about Preferences](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/preferences)

Organization preferences are controlled from the Notification Categories page on the SuprSend dashboard.

You can manage Brand and User preferences programmatically using the HTTP API methods listed in the next sections

item.name: Tenants
item.description:
If you send notifications on behalf of your customers to their end users, you might be tasked with handling custom styling in the messages. This can be quite cumbersome if you have to maintain these customisation for every brand in your codebase.

Brands empower you to send personalized communication on behalf of your customers using a single API. You just have to store brand guidelines like logo, name, colors, social links and other custom properties for your customers once and then use your brand variables in templates to dynamically render the template for each of your customer.

[Learn more about tenants](https://docs.suprsend.com/docs/brands)

item.description:
You can use these methods in sequence to replace list users with a new set of users completely.

- [Start Sync](https://www.postman.com/blue-space-557703/workspace/suprsend/request/27786422-1b6075c3-fce2-45ee-bae6-d55c384e2356) : This will create a new draft version of the list where you can sync the new set of users.
    
- [Add Subscribers to Draft List](https://www.postman.com/blue-space-557703/workspace/suprsend/request/27786422-277c8ec5-2afe-4ddf-90ea-6e1e3e313787): Once the draft is created, you can add users to the draft with this method.
    
- [Remove Subscribers from Draft List](https://www.postman.com/blue-space-557703/workspace/suprsend/request/27786422-4894457e-e794-4f76-b707-2e1e5a56d408): You can remove users from the draft version using this method.
    
- [Finish Sync](https://www.postman.com/blue-space-557703/workspace/suprsend/request/27786422-ced03eeb-d66e-40c4-ae65-3e09cfe482db): Once all your new users are added in the draft version. You can call this method to finish sync. The draft version will become live after the sync is finished and all the new broadcasts will be sent on the replaced user set.

item.name: Broadcast

request.description:
## Request Body Params

_**workflow**_ : workflow_slug | string | required field. You can get workflow slug from workflow settings on SuprSend dashboard.

_**recipients**_: array of objects | required. List of recipients to be notified. You can either add recipient as array of distinct_ids or array of recipient objects. You can add up to 100 recipients in a single API.

_**actor**_: json object | required. Includes distinct_id and properties of the user who performed the action. You can use it for cross-user notifications where you need to include actor properties in the notification template. Actor properties can be added as $actor..

_**data**_: json object. Variable data required to render dynamic template content or workflow properties like dynamic delay or channel override in send node.

_**tenant_id**_: string. String identifier of the brand/tenant this workflow is associated with. Used to trigger multi-tenant notifications.

_**$idempotency_key**_: string. Idempotency_key (valid for 24hrs).

## Headers

_**authorization:**_ suprsend APIs use bearer authorization. to send a successful request, one muse set the correct the _api_key_ value in the variables. To learn more about how to generate the _api_key_ refer [this.](https://docs.suprsend.com/reference/api-keys)

item.description:
The Management API provides comprehensive control over workflow lifecycle management, allowing you to list, get, create/update, delete, enable/disable, and commit workflows programmatically across your workspaces.

All workflow changes are saved as drafts and require explicit commitment to become live, ensuring safe deployment without affecting production workflows.
